media_item.focus_or_theme: DNA exoneration after decades of imprisonment; Eyewitness misidentification.
media_item.summary_notes: This 60 Minutes segment focuses on Cornelius Dupree Jr.'s wrongful conviction and exoneration after serving 30 years. It highlights the issues of eyewitness misidentification and the impact of wrongful convictions on individuals and their families.
key_quotes_raw: Cornelius Dupree: "words really won't make up for what I lost... I lost both my parents uh I just feel that you know the system need to be fixed..."
Highlighting that Dupree refused parole because it required admitting guilt/registering as a sex offender.
systemic_issues_raw: Personal toll of wrongful conviction (loss of family)
policy_recommendations_raw: Dupree calls for systemic fixes to prevent similar cases.

featured_individuals.crime_convicted_of_raw: Aggravated Robbery (stemming from a 1979 rape/carjacking incident; never tried for rape)
featured_individuals.narrative_summary: Cornelius Dupree Jr. was wrongfully convicted of aggravated robbery in 1980 and sentenced to 75 years. He was exonerated by DNA evidence in 2011 after serving 30 years. The case highlights eyewitness misidentification as a contributing factor to his wrongful conviction.
contributing_factors_raw: Eyewitness misidentification (one victim identified him, another did not)
organizations_involved_raw: Dallas County District Attorney's Conviction Integrity Unit
